title: Xenoblade Chronicles X
subtitle: Human survivors on an unfamiliar planet
summary: Xenoblade Chronicles X is Monolith Soft's open-world role-playing game, first released for Wii U in Japan on 29 April 2015.
body: Xenoblade Chronicles X is Monolith Soft's open-world role-playing game, first released for Wii U in Japan on 29 April 2015. Survivors of Earth's destruction establish New Los Angeles on the planet Mira, and the player's created character joins BLADE to explore and protect their new home. Five continents surround the settlement with enormous creatures, striking terrain and signs of other civilizations. The journey makes discovery a practical task for the surviving community, connecting the next expedition to humanity's effort to understand where it has landed.

Exploration, quests and resource gathering build the relationship between the city and the wider planet. The party moves through Mira's changing environments while real-time battles combine ordinary attacks with selected Arts and other systems. Learning a creature's strength or finding a route through an unfamiliar region matters to deciding which objective can be attempted next. The open landscape lets distant sights become long-term destinations, with the player's growing capabilities gradually turning the outline of the world into places that can actually be reached.

Skells add pilotable machines that change both travel and combat, eventually opening flight across terrain first encountered from the ground. Hiroyuki Sawano composed the soundtrack. Production began after Xenoblade Chronicles, with Tetsuya Takahashi and returning staff pursuing a much larger explorable world. The original Wii U version reached Western audiences that December; an expanded Definitive Edition followed on Switch in 2025. Its defining progression is spatial as well as statistical: the same planet acquires another scale when a route once crossed on foot can be seen and traveled from above.
